visual_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 more accurately visualizes the full projectile-motion situation with a ground-to-ground parabolic path, launch components, landing point, and flight-time derivation, while Lesson 1’s shown frame is correct for velocity decomposition but is less complete and does not visually represent the range/trajectory aspect of the problem.

interactivity.rationale: Lesson 2 has a real, wired fill-in gate after act_decomposition with a concrete prompt, accepted answer, hint, and remediation path, while Lesson 1 has no available gate specs or plan and must be treated as having no functioning interactivity.

narration_quality.rationale: Lesson 2 has smoother, more natural phrasing and structured pacing with clear spoken math, while Lesson 1 is understandable but starts abruptly with a missing subject and feels more densely delivered in a single explanatory stream.

sync.rationale: Lesson 2 provides timed visual cues that mostly appear near the narration references, while Lesson 1 has no beat/timing data or cues at all, so its on-screen changes cannot be verified as synchronized with the narration.

concept_accuracy.rationale: Lesson 2 is mathematically correct like Lesson 1 but teaches the concept more clearly by deriving the flight-time equation, explicitly connecting vertical and horizontal motion, and reinforcing component reasoning, whereas Lesson 1 gives the correct solution but relies more on stated formulas with less pedagogical unpacking.

polish.rationale: Lesson 2 has a much cleaner, centered, consistent full-frame presentation, while Lesson 1 is marred by visible browser/video UI overlays, excessive empty space, a faint nearly invisible subtitle on the title screen, and a mid-lesson layout with an oversized mostly empty box and off-balance diagram placement.

aggregator.explanation: All six dimension agents prefer Lesson 2, with consistently high confidence. Lesson 2 is judged more visually complete and accurate, substantially more interactive, better narrated, better synchronized, more pedagogically clear in its concept development, and more polished in presentation. Since every dimension favors Lesson 2 and several do so strongly, there is a clear overall winner rather than a tie.
